cabecera.pregunta: What should I plant next year?
cabecera.sub: A season does not end at harvest: the soil keeps less water, and fungi and pests that overwinter. With 25 years of NASA climate data we show what this year left behind in your area and which rotation reduces it.

nasa.texto: We compare each season with the ones before it using NASA POWER temperature, humidity and rainfall. It describes your area, not your field, and it does not confirm disease.
nasa.detalle: NASA POWER: 219,144 hours of temperature and humidity (2001–2025) and 16,436 days of rainfall and temperature (1981–2025).
nasa.fuente: NASA POWER (MERRA-2 / GEOS-IT), celda de ~0.5 x 0.625 grados

textos.aviso: This tool helps you compare. It does not predict disease or replace what you and your advisor know about the field.
textos.leyenda: Levels compare options with each other; they are not the probability of disease.
textos.celda: NASA data measures an area about 50 km wide. It does not see your field on its own.

agua.texto_estado: The soil is full of water (as of 2025-12-31).
agua.texto_anio: In 2025 there were 51 thirsty days for corn; the usual is 45.
limites: Rain and temperature for a cell of about 50 km; not the field.
All rain enters the soil (no runoff): heavy rain can make thirst look lower than it was.
Each crop is calculated as if planted every year, with no carry-over between crops.
Root depth and crop coefficients (Kc) are fixed: they are assumptions.
The organic-matter adjustment is a sensitivity assumption, not a measurement.
agua.texto_metodo: This is an estimate: it uses NASA POWER daily rain and temperature plus crop and soil parameters. It does not measure your field's moisture.
agua.texto_rango: Depending on how much water your soil holds (110–180 mm per meter for silt loam), 2025 would have between 36 and 61 thirsty days.
